title: refactor: Make command implementations responsible for logging the `version` JSON log at the start of execution.
body:
Alternative solution to https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/39215

# Problem

There are a few times where we want/need to initialise a view partway through a command's execution. However, there's a problem in those situations as initialising a (SRO-style) JSON view implementation causes a version log to be produced.

That's fine if you only initialise the JSON view once at the start of the command, but if you need to initialise a new view partway through you'll end up with duplicate version log entries in unexpected positions in the log output.

Times when a secondary views are initialised include:
1. Scenarios during `init` where deeply nested code needs to log output but a view it's tunnelled through those layers of nesting.
    *  See code: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/b6e97ff8a4fd22ac938866adf47d3e556b90b18a/internal/command/meta_backend.go#L1617
2. Using a StateLocker view during commands that lock the state.
    * Example of this in use: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/b6e97ff8a4fd22ac938866adf47d3e556b90b18a/internal/command/state_mv.go#L107


In scenario 1 there is currently a second version log that's produced, in scenario 2 there are no instances of that problem _yet_ but I want to protect against the problem being accidentally added in future.

# Proposal

We make commands responsible for invoking a `Version` command to create the version log, if the command produces SRO-style JSON output.
